subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm deciding to keep this simple by skipping joints entirely since it's a static vehicle model, which reduces risk and complexity.

Now I'm designing an armored wheeled interceptor around 5.2m long with four large wheels, an armored hull, cabin, roof turret with water cannon, neon light bars, bull bar, and decal-covered side plates. I'm planning a gunmetal and neon cyberpunk color palette along with SVG textures for a fictional "VANTA SECURITY" logo, hazard stripes, tinted windshield, grille, and HUD screen details.

Writing wheel geometry...

Actually, a simpler approach: extrude the entire side-profile silhouette of the car body along the x-axis to get the full shape in one pass, rather than assembling separate boxes. I'm sketching the profile points in the z-y plane -- rear, nose, hood, windshield, roof, and tail -- then extruding that outline with thickness along x for the car's width.

Still working out the hull and cabin as separate extrusions, plus positioning a tinted windshield plane angled along the slope between hood and roof, computing its normal and size from the profile geometry.

Now I'm placing side window planes on the cabin flanks as narrow armored slits with dark tinted glass and cyan reflections, working out their offsets and dimensions along the body.

I'm defining the cabin and hull cross-section profiles as polygon coordinate points, then checking that wheel positions and widths fit cleanly within the hull's outer edges without clipping.

I'm adding fender boxes positioned just above each wheel to cover them, sizing them to extend slightly beyond the wheel width, then planning a roof turret with a lathe-based cylindrical base, a forward-facing water cannon barrel with a glowing nozzle tip, and considering where to place a water tank on the rear deck.

Now I'm placing the turret toward the rear of the roof, angling the barrel upward and forward over the windshield with a flared nozzle cone and cyan glow ring, adding side hoses and a radar dish with antenna, then positioning a glowing light bar across the front of the cabin roof.

I'm adding underbody and side neon strips along the hull flanks, a full-width rear light bar, angular glowing headlights with cyan daytime running lines, and a dark front bull bar with grille texture, now working out the nose's sloped front face geometry.

umper box plus a hazard decal plane. Now I'm working out side plates for the hull flanks with text reading "VANTA // CIVIL SUPPRESSION UNIT" plus a logo, figuring out orientation so the text doesn't mirror when facing outward—computing local axes from the up vector crossed with the facing direction to get the correct right-vector for each plane.

Now I'm designing the side panel texture with door seams, a "RIOT CONTROL" label, logo, hazard stripe, and unit number, sizing it to fit the flank of the hull at the appropriate height and depth offset.

For the body paint, I'm writing a procedural shader function that blends a dark navy-gunmetal base with panel lines and grime wear near the bottom using noise and smoothstep, mixing colors defined as RGB strings. I'm also planning the rear details—doors, light bar, exhaust placeholder, and a "VANTA" logo plane positioned at the rear hull face with its orientation computed from the up and forward vectors.

Now I'm adding roof extras: a full-width front light bar near the roof slope, a rear roof bar, side rails, antenna rods with glowing tips, camera pods with red glowing eyes at the front corners, and roof-mounted spotlights. I'm also placing mirror pods on the cabin sides, a glowing neon-style sign on the turret flank, and figuring out a thin cyan underglow box beneath the hull bottom.

I'm designing the water cannon system: a lathed turret base, an angular extruded turret body, a reinforced barrel with banded cylinders, a rear horizontal tank with hazard-stripe paint and "H2O" labeling, support cylinders, and a swept hose connecting the tank to the turret nozzle, which glows cyan.

Now I'm working out the turret geometry — rotating base at the roof's rear, a boxy turret body around y 2.1-2.55, and a tapered barrel extending forward and slightly upward past the windshield height, ending in a flared nozzle, keeping overall height around 3.0 units for the armored truck profile.

I'm sketching helper functions for boxes, glowing neon edges, and cylinders, then planning to mirror these across the sides to keep the model symmetric without relying on text or decals that might not render reliably.

Designing texture-based plane parts with optional glow, a tinted glass gradient texture with cyan streaks, and SVG definitions for hazard stripes and a hex-shield corporate logo.

Still writing SVG panels...

Writing tire paint function...

For the hull I'm setting up a paint function that mixes dark base colors depending on lighting angle, adds grime toward the bottom, and draws panel seam lines using fractional position patterns along the body.

For the cabin, I'm picking a two-tone cyberpunk scheme: dark steel blue upper cabin, gunmetal hull, yellow trim accents with cyan/magenta neon highlights, plus a yellow chevron decal on the sloped hood surface aligned to the nose's slope geometry.

Now I'm planning neon accent strips along the side hull in magenta and cyan, then deciding to skip detailed wheel arch lighting for scope. I'm targeting around 200 parts through repeated bolts, vents, and rivets rather than the full 180-340 range, prioritizing quality, and still need to add push bar prongs, tow hook, side steps, door handles, and window mesh bars.

Adding sirens, light bar, rear spoiler pods, side armor rib plates in yellow, and camera pods with glowing red lenses on the front corners plus a sensor mast on the roof. I'm now setting up the imports from the agentic-3js-builder SDK and its glow kit before defining color constants.

Working through the extrude call for the hull outline, mapping coordinates so x aligns with z, with sharp bevel corners. Then I'm placing wheel positions for a heavier truck with three axles, spacing the rear dual wheels carefully so they don't overlap given the wheel diameter.

Adding fender boxes over each wheel, sized and positioned to slightly overlap the hull sides, plus thin dark mudguard flaps behind the wheels. I'm checking that the hull bottom height and wheel radius mean the wheels only extend past the hull sides where the hull narrows.

I'm placing half-sphere siren domes on the roof using a sphere geometry capped at the equator, then adding a light bar on the front roof as a dark box positioned where the cabin roof profile is nearly flat near the front.

Now I'm segmenting the light bar into alternating cyan/magenta glowing boxes, mirroring a second bar at the rear, and checking clearances between the turret, barrel, and both bars so nothing overlaps -- repositioning the rear bar further back where the roof slopes to avoid colliding with the tank's rear end.

Building the turret structure...

Still shaping the nozzle geometry...

Now I'm adding a glowing cyan ring near the nozzle, plus a HUD-style glow panel on the turret sides and a neon strip accent. I'm also laying out curved hose connectors sweeping from the tank sides up to the turret rear using arced control points.

For the tank itself, I'm orienting it horizontally with a rounded cylinder body, applying a custom paint shader that bands the ends in hazard yellow while keeping the mid-section a weathered blue, and adding darker end caps plus a glowing cyan water-level window strip.

Now I'm placing rooftop details: antenna rods at the rear corners with small glowing magenta tips, and considering a lathe-built satellite dish off to one side.

I'm shaping the dish's bowl profile and tilting its axis, then moving to the front end to build the bumper and bull-bar prongs as vertical rods sitting in a box shape near the hull's front.

I'm positioning the bumper with dark metal and a hazard plane up front, then sketching a push bar frame with a top rail and support rods, checking that it doesn't clip into the headlights positioned near the grille.

For the bull bar, I'm placing curved uprights near the bumper leading to the hood front with a crossbar grille guard, then designing the headlights with a glowing housing, cyan DRL strip below, and a darker angular backing.

Now for the rear end, I'm adding a magenta light bar across the rear face, a logo plane, and a door seam texture plane, but checking the vertical positioning since the bar and plane overlap — need to shift the bar up slightly to fit under the hull's top edge.

I'm also placing a rear bumper box and corner taillight clusters with red-magenta glow, then working out the cabin's side window geometry by solving for the slope intersection along the pillar face.

Now I'm splitting the cabin windows into front and rear sections separated by a B-pillar, adding door seams, side mirrors with stalks, and sizing the tinted windshield plane.

Adding wipers, a visor brow over the windshield, hood vents, and side ribs on the hull while leaving gaps for the wheel fenders.

I'm realizing the wheel positions actually overlap the hull side panel region, leaving only a narrow strip free for the side panel detail. I should push the wheels further outward so their inner face clears the hull side, keeping real wheel wells above the panel line like an actual armored truck.

Shifting to two axle positions at z 1.55 and -1.5 opens up nearly 2 meters of clear side panel space, so I'll size the panel at 1.9 x 0.55 to fit there.

Writing SVG code...

I'm also planning skirt armor plates as simple boxes near the wheel flanks, plus a subtle cyan underglow box tucked beneath the hull bottom so it's mostly hidden except from low angles, and small roof vents with a hatch detail. Now I'm settling on the color palette: steel gray, dark near-black, warning yellow, and cyan accents.

Writing paint shader logic...

Still defining tire tread and sidewall patterns...

Now I'm designing the window reflection gradient, the hexagonal logo with a yellow "V" and cyan ring arcs, the hazard stripe pattern, and the chevron markings, each as separate SVG textures.

For the grille I'm adding dark slit lines with a weak cyan glow overlay so the dark parts stay dark, then the HUD readout showing "H2O 87%" over cyan bars, and the rear panel with door lines, "VANTA / CIVIL ORDER DIVISION" text, and a plate reading "NC-4471" on a transparent background.

Now I'm positioning a small glowing logo on both turret flanks just above the HUD, sizing and stacking the HUD and logo panels against the body height, then setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, rods, and planes to build out the model.

For planes I'm handling orientation with dir and up vectors depending on whether it's angled like a hood or facing sideways, and making sure textured parts use standard materials for glow compatibility. I'm mirroring parts across the left/right sides, adding cabin side windows, and building mirror pods with stalks and dark housing boxes, possibly with a small glowing strip.

Now I'm adding side steps between the wheels, door handles positioned on the body panels, and front camera pods near the hood corners with small glowing red dots, plus thinking through vent slots on the hood.

Adding rivet details to the bumper and wheel hubs, then starting the wheel-building function with tire cylinders rotated to align with the axle.

Checking tire and fender extents against the model dimensions to confirm nothing clips, then working out the barrel's direction vector for the lathe-based nozzle geometry and its glowing disc cap at the muzzle end.

Now I'm deciding on the turret's paint scheme—leaning toward a yellow-accented body with grime blended in rather than plain dark panels, using a color mix function for the lit/shaded tones, and adding a rod-based barrel with colored bands for visual detail.

I'm also working through implementation details: a bodyPaint helper for seams and grime, checking noise and mix function signatures, and making sure plain number arrays type-check correctly for vector positions. Now I'm placing the windshield normal and center point, and thinking about adding thin vertical dark bars across the side windows to simulate slats.

Finishing the detail work: adding window bars, a windshield wiper, and a roof brow, then placing siren domes on the roof as small glowing hemispheres with cylinder bases, positioned to the sides of the central turret. Ready to write the final code.
